newsitem.title: FRANCE: All foreigners out of Brazzaville soon - French army.
newsitem.headline: All foreigners out of Brazzaville soon - French army.

text.p: The French military said on Friday it expected to have evacuated all French nationals and most other foreign civilians from the embattled Congo capital Brazzaville within two days.

"In another 36 to 48 hours, we will have pulled out all the French and most of the other foreigners from Brazza," a military spokesman told Reuters. He did not say how many foreigners remained to be pulled out.
"Then we will be in a position where we can pull out our forces," the officer added.

He said the French troops, operating out of Brazzaville airport and making forays into the city to rescue endangered foreigners, had so far flown 3,420 foreign civilians, 1,410 of them French, out of the country.
France has said that its troops in the Congo, over 1,250 foreign legionnaires and marine paratroops, would not intervene in the fighting and were on the spot to protect foreigners.
The spokesman said the intensity of fighting between forces loyal to President Pascal Lissouba and those of his Marxist predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso had eased during the night.
The conflict erupted after soldiers surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on private militias before the July 27 presidential election.
